<description>
IsRoutable() doesn't exclude multicast (224.0.0.0/4, ff00::/8), so multicast addresses received over gossip can end up in addrman.

This adds IsMulticast() and excludes it in IsRoutable().

Test updates:
- addrman_getaddr: expected counts change, since its generated addresses include the multicast range.
- The last asmap test vector was a multicast address. I replaced it with a non-multicast one at the top of the range (same AS).
</description>

<commits>
d54f486882 netaddress: don't treat multicast addresses as routable

IsRoutable() excluded private, documentation, link-local and other
special ranges, but not multicast (224.0.0.0/4, ff00::/8). Gossiped
multicast addresses were therefore accepted into addrman and could be
selected for outbound connections.

Add CNetAddr::IsMulticast() and exclude it in IsRoutable().

addrman_getaddr generates addresses with every first octet, so the
expected counts drop by the multicast ones. The last asmap test vector
was an ff00::/8 address, which now maps to AS0 as unroutable; use a
non-multicast address at the top of the range instead (same AS).
</commits>
